root_idea.summary: The root centers on cutting or severing, especially detaching a part from its whole.
root_idea.development: The lexical range extends from cutting a part away or plucking it from its root to the detached piece, the state of becoming severed, and the sharp cutting quality of an instrument.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested Form II verb is presented under its normalized perfect-tense dictionary citation form.

senses.definition: To cut off or sever a part, especially by cutting it from its root; in the Quranic construction, to cut or slit the ears of cattle.
senses.usage_conditions: Active Form II; the doubled form may convey extensive or repeated action, or its application to multiple objects. The attested Quranic construction concerns the ears of cattle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pluck out hair, feathers, or the like by grasping and pulling them until they are detached from the root.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive use describing removal by pulling rather than merely cutting across.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become cut, severed, or detached, entirely or from the root; also, to become plucked out.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Intransitive Form VII construction describing the resulting state of severance or detachment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A piece or portion cut off or severed; by extension, a portion of the latter part of the night, especially its remaining darkness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also attested with the variant pronunciation بَتْكَةٌ; plural بِتَكٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An epithet meaning sharp or cutting; بَتُوكٌ is an intensive form meaning very sharp or keenly cutting.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited application is to a sword or other cutting instrument; بَتُوكٌ intensifies the description.
